findings.source_passage: I wonder whether those jolly lads bethink them of what they are dancing over. I'll dance over your grave, I will—that's the bitterest threat of your night-women
findings.why_it_matters: The Old Manx Sailor's meditation is one of the chapter's interpretive keystones—the 'dance over your grave' formulation is distinctive and carries the ominous undercurrent of the whole scene; the draft collapses it to a bare summary.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the Manx Sailor's speech closer to verbatim: 'I wonder whether those jolly lads bethink them of what they are dancing over. I'll dance over your grave, I will—that's the bitterest threat of your night-women…'

findings.source_passage: Ready formed. There! the ringed horizon. In that ring Cain struck Abel. Sweet work, right work! No? Why then, God, mad'st thou the ring?
findings.source_locator: Old Manx Sailor's second speech, during the fight
findings.why_it_matters: This is one of the most critically noted speeches in the chapter—the Cain/Abel allusion within 'the ringed horizon' is a signature theological aside that carries heavy interpretive weight about violence and divine complicity; it is entirely absent from the draft.
findings.suggested_fix: Insert the Old Manx Sailor's ring speech during the brawl scene: 'Ready formed. There! the ringed horizon. In that ring Cain struck Abel. Sweet work, right work! No? Why then, God, mad'st thou the ring?'

findings.source_passage: it makes me jingle all over like my tambourine—that anaconda of an old man swore 'em in to hunt him!
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'anaconda of an old man' and 'jingle all over like my tambourine' are signature Pip-voice coinages; the draft retains 'anaconda' but omits the tambourine simile, losing the self-reflexive, voice-defining character of the speech.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'it makes me jingle all over like my tambourine—that anaconda of an old man swore 'em in to hunt him!' verbatim within Pip's closing monologue.

findings.source_passage: 2ND NANTUCKET SAILOR. Avast the chorus!… Star-bo-l-e-e-n-s, a-h-o-y! Eight bells there below! Tumble up!
findings.why_it_matters: The phonetic rendering of the sailor's bellow ('Star-bo-l-e-e-n-s, a-h-o-y!') is a period/register marker and a small comic-voice moment; its complete omission erases some of the chapter's nautical texture.
findings.suggested_fix: Include at least the phonetically spelled shout to preserve the register flavor of the scene.

summary: The draft's most serious failure is the complete omission of the Old Manx Sailor's 'ringed horizon / Cain struck Abel' speech, an interpretively critical passage; combined with two further medium-severity flattenings of the Manx Sailor's first speech and Pip's tambourine simile, the threshold for regeneration is met.
